fixes.explanation: Close to the neighborhood, but no, friend. Verses 14 and 15 are where the words about serving God being futile show up. The scroll is about “…those who feared the LORD and honored His name.” That's who spoke with one another and got heard.

Leap! The LORD says, “…you will go out and leap like calves from the stall.” Picture the door swinging open and everybody bouncing out. I can hop and dive face-first into the chocolate chips, gold base and all, but these folks do it way better.

That's right. The LORD says, “Remember the law of My servant Moses, the statutes and ordinances I commanded him for all Israel at Horeb.” Moses was Israel's leader (Exodus 3:10). The word is remember, friend, and it's for all Israel.

David, Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3), is a fine servant to think of, friend. But he isn't in these verses. The LORD says, “Remember the law of My servant Moses…” It's the statutes and ordinances He commanded Moses for all Israel.

Joseph, one of Jacob's sons (Genesis 35:24), isn't named here, friend. The LORD is the one speaking, and He says, “Remember the law of My servant Moses, the statutes and ordinances I commanded him for all Israel at Horeb.” No dreams in this verse, just the law.

Yes, friend. The LORD says, “Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and awesome Day of the LORD.” He sends him before the Day comes. That's a prophet showing up ahead of the main event.

Samuel was a prophet (1 Samuel 3:20), friend, but he isn't the name in this verse. The LORD says, “…I will send you Elijah the prophet…” That's the one He sends before the great and awesome Day of the LORD.

Isaiah was a prophet too (2 Kings 19:2), friend, but the name here is different. The LORD says, “…I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and awesome Day of the LORD.” It's good to know your prophets, though. Plenty of names on that list.

Prophets aren't the hearts being turned here, friend. The verse says Elijah “…will turn the hearts of the fathers to their children, and the hearts of the children to their fathers.” They turn toward each other, one way and then the other.
